doc.title: John Heard interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Dance and magic in music, not math
summary: Heard says where he plays does not matter; his concept is dance and magic, a view Woods compares to Copland's remark, and he says he is not a dancer.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: From the places you’ve been in the country, is there places you’d rather not play or places you would rather play? I mean is it pretty much the same?
Yeah. It has nothing to do with magic. Drop me off anywhere. We’ll have fun.
Well you ought to sell some of that then.

Oh, yeah, that’s what I do every time I get on the bandstand, man, yeah, that’s it. That’s my concept. The dance and the magic. There’s nothing else. There’s no math, there’s no Hindemith, and none of that crap. It’s all about dance and magic, a smile.

You know Aaron Copland was asked to judge a contest of twentieth century music one day. And they asked him they said, “What do you think of most of the scores that come in from the competition?” He says, “Very little of it sings or dances.” I think that’s what you’re trying to say. It’s gotta sing, it’s got to dance.
Yeah, that’s right. It’s what Ellington made remarks on one time or another.
I can run though. No I can’t dance. I mean I can clown around but I don’t take it anywhere. I’m not a dancer. Maybe that’s something I should work on.
